newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise gains on bullish executive speech.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise gains on bullish executive speech.

text.p: Shares in oil exploration and production firm Enterprise Oil Plc gained 20 pence to 558, the highest level this year, following an upbeat speech delivered yesterday in the U.S. by group managing director Mike Pink, analysts said.
Speaking at an oil conference in New Orleans, Pink said the recoverable reserves of the Norwegian Valhall oil field, in which Enterprise has a 28.1 percent interest, may rise significantly.
"Recoverable reserves are now at 580 million barrels and we believe there is significantly more to come," Pink said in the speech made available by Enterprise to Reuters in London.
"With continued innovation...our people tell me that future additions may exceed another 200 million barrels, ultimately giving us a field with more than a billion barrels recoverable," he added.
Analysts, many of them already positive on Enterprise, said the comments helped sentiment, although one said: "It's potential rather than in the bag at the moment."
Operator Amoco Norway A/S said in November last year that the combined recoverable reserves of Valhall and the Hod field could eventually total one billion barrels.
Referring to Amoco's remarks, an Enterprise spokeswoman played down the news content of Pink's speech.
"It is just something... that could possibly happen in the future, but it would take a long time to get there," she said.
Valhall is Enterprise's main asset in Norway. The company also has promising operations in Italy where analysts will visit the Val d'Agri field early next month.
